1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Be7 5.O-.strategy: Prepares the double fianchetto after castling: both bishops will aim at the centre and the c4-pawn is supported, so Black cannot win it. White avoids committing the d-pawn and keeps the position flexible, a slower but safe plan.
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Be7 5.O-.name: English Opening: Agincourt Defence, Neo-Catalan Declined

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Be7 5.O-.strategy: Strikes at d4 at once, so White cannot easily build a centre there, and keeps the c-pawn active instead of tucking it away on c6. Black accepts a more open, more dynamic game in which the d5-pawn needs watching but the pieces have room.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Be7 5.O-.strategy: Reinforces d5 with a pawn and keeps the structure compact and hard to attack. The price is passivity: the c8-bishop stays shut in behind the chain, so Black has a very safe position but little counterplay until it is freed.
